questions: You narrowed your hypothesis from 'does an agent managing its own memory improve consistency' to 'does recall of a prior ruling improve consistency' — what made you decide that tradeoff was worth it rather than trying to fix the agent's write access issue first?

In your test design, you had to pivot from a 14-run batch to just four runs on purpose-built claims because the memory wasn't finding anything to recall — what signal told you this was a setup problem rather than evidence that memory wouldn't help?

You discovered the agent was picking and ruling on the wrong claim before the target was specified, then added the claim name to the injected message — but you note that claim identity now lives in two places with no enforcement. Why accept that divergence risk rather than enforce it structurally?
